provenance.instrument: Clifton Heights Borough Zoning Ordinance of 1993 (Chapter 340 Zoning, Ord. No. 729 of 3-22-1993, as amended), with Chapter 165 Floodplain Management (Ord. No. 846 of 10-20-2015), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CL3044, Borough of Clifton Heights, PA. 340-112A sends appeals to the Court of Common Pleas of Delaware County and 340-115D(2) uses the Delaware County Tax Assessment Office, so this is Clifton Heights borough, Delaware County. The district use lists and figures are web text in each district article. Attachment 1 (Appendix A, C-1 areas), Attachment 2 (Zoning Requirements) and Attachment 3 (Table of Permitted Uses) are PDF summaries that were not opened. The latest amendments seen are Ord. Nos. 866, 868 and 869 of 2019. New Laws lists no new law
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows 'Includes legislation through 12-17-2019.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
provenance.code_caution: The online code includes legislation only through 12-17-2019. Its New Laws list is empty, and no later zoning amendment was found, but one may exist. Ask the borough office whether Chapter 340 has changed since 2019
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. A search for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, guest house, living quarters, conversion, two-family, granny, elder cottage, temporary dwelling and apartment found the dwelling and conversion definitions, the R-2 and R-3 two-family listings and the I district conversion of industrial buildings (340-53C)

R-1 is used 'by right only' for a single-family detached dwelling and municipal uses, with schools, religious uses, day care, clubs and cluster development by special exception (340-14, 340-15). R-2 adds semidetached, attached (at most five in a row) and two-family dwellings of three kinds, including 'Two-family detached or a duplex dwelling containing no more than two single-family dwellings' (340-19). R-3 adds multifamily dwellings on one acre (340-24). The RCZ cluster option is a special exception on a tract of one acre (340-28 to 340-31). RCD permits recreation uses, with low-density single-family dwellings at seven units per acre by special exception (340-35, 340-36). C-1, C-2 and I list no dwelling

Accessory uses in the residential districts are parking and private garages, 'Utility sheds, toolsheds and similar accessory structures', pools, signs, home occupations and decks (340-16, 340-21, 340-26). A dwelling unit is 'One or more rooms designed constituting a separate housekeeping unit which, at a minimum, must include cooking, sleeping and sanitary facilities'. A family is persons related by blood, marriage or adoption, or no more than three unrelated persons, living as a single housekeeping unit (340-12)

Accessory structures cover at most 5% of the lot in residential districts, are at most one story or 14 ft tall, stand at least 3 ft from the side and rear lines 'and behind the rearmost portion of the principal building', and on a corner lot no closer to the side street than the house (340-80). The district sections keep them out of the required front yard and 5 ft from any property line, reducible to 3 ft by special exception (340-17I, 340-22J, 340-27J)

Lot area: 5,000 sq ft per single-family detached dwelling in R-1, 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit for residential uses in R-2, the R-2 figure in R-3 except 1,500 sq ft per unit for attached and multifamily uses (340-17A, 340-22A, 340-27A). A lot held in single and separate ownership when the chapter took effect may be built on below the minimum area or width if the use, yard, setback and density rules are met (340-102)

Parking: 'Single-family dwelling, 2 per dwelling unit', and for multifamily and townhouses 1 space for an efficiency, 2 for one or two bedrooms and 3 for three or more. Only a fraction of 1/2 or more counts as a space. The table has no two-family row. Parking is on the same lot except in C-1. A use changed or extended so that it needs more parking provides the added spaces (340-67C, 340-68)

Floodplain (Chapter 165, FIRM of November 18, 2009, applied through 340-8): new construction and substantial improvements of residential structures are elevated to the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, basements are prohibited, and an accessory structure that is not elevated is not used for habitation and is at most 200 sq ft. In the floodway nothing may raise flood levels and new construction needs a DEP permit. Manufactured homes are prohibited unless a variance is granted, and never within 50 ft of the top of bank. The Borough decides floodplain variances, and appeals of the Floodplain Administrator go to the Zoning Hearing Board (165-17, 165-19, 165-24, 165-28, 165-33, 165-34)

Riparian buffer: 'The riparian buffer shall be maintained within 100 feet of the top of stream bank and shall remain as open, undeveloped area' (340-87G). Steep slopes (over 15%), wetlands and riparian buffers are deducted from the area used for total improvement coverage (340-12). No steep slope or wetland chapter was found in Chapter 340

Special exceptions are granted only where the district article provides for them, with an environmental impact assessment and a traffic impact study (340-114, 340-90, 340-90.1). A use variance also needs an environmental impact assessment (340-90A). Variances go to the Zoning Hearing Board on the MPC findings, and lapse without a building permit within six months (340-105C, 340-109A, 340-111). No bar on a use variance was found

Nonconforming uses and structures may be enlarged by special exception once, by at most 50%, within the district's area, height and setback rules (340-98). In I, the conversion of existing industrial buildings to residential units is a special exception (340-53C)

term.note: Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, guest house, living quarters, conversion, two-family, granny, elder cottage, temporary dwelling and apartment. No ADU use. The nearest are the two-family dwellings of R-2 and R-3 (340-19D to F)

status.note: No district lists a second unit on a house lot. R-1 is used 'by right only' for a single-family detached dwelling and municipal uses. R-2 and R-3 permit two-family dwellings by right

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In R-2 and R-3 a house may instead become a two-family dwelling by right where the lot has 3,000 sq ft per unit (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the MPC findings. No bar on a use variance was found

unlisted_use_path.note: Only I lets the Zoning Hearing Board allow a use of the same general character as its listed industrial and service uses. RCD allows a use of the same general character as its recreation uses by conditional use (340-35.1B). Elsewhere a use not listed needs a use variance. I lists no dwelling, while R-2 and R-3 list two-family dwellings, so in those districts a second unit is read as that listed use, not an unlisted one

unlisted_use_districts.note: The other districts are used 'by right only' for their listed uses

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Those uses not specifically permitted by right, but of the same general character as those listed in § 340-52 above

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: R-2 permits by right a 'Two-family detached or a duplex dwelling containing no more than two single-family dwellings', a two-family semidetached dwelling and a two-family attached dwelling, and R-3 permits every R-2 use. The lot needs 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, so 6,000 sq ft for two units, and a two-family detached dwelling 50 ft of width. Two side yards of 8 ft and 20 ft together, front 20 ft, rear 25 ft, building coverage 30% in R-2 and 50% in R-3, height 35 ft. Parking is 2 spaces per single-family dwelling unit and the table has no two-family row. A changed or extended use provides the added parking. Each unit has its own cooking, sleeping and sanitary facilities
value.note: The code has no conversion section, so whether an existing house may be changed into a two-family dwelling under these listings is read from 340-75A (a change of use in conformity with the chapter). Ask the zoning officer

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. R-2 and R-3 list two-family dwellings. RCD lists low-density single-family dwellings by special exception, and I the conversion of industrial buildings to residential units by special exception

value.condition: In the identified floodplain an accessory structure that is not elevated or floodproofed 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', is limited to parking or storage, has at most 200 sq ft of floor area and no sanitary facilities or permanently affixed utility equipment. Floodplain variances are decided by the Borough under Chapter 165, with no variance that raises the base flood elevation.

In the identified floodplain any new construction or substantial improvement of a residential structure has its lowest floor, basement included, at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, and basements are prohibited. Work under 50% of market value is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible. No expansion of an existing structure may raise the base flood elevation. New construction is a structure begun on or after September 1, 2015, with its later improvements.

In the floodway no encroachment, fill, new construction, substantial improvement or other development is permitted unless a hydrologic and hydraulic analysis shows no increase in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a permit from the DEP Regional Office.

'The riparian buffer shall be maintained within 100 feet of the top of stream bank and shall remain as open, undeveloped area.' A new building or addition for the unit cannot stand within 100 ft of the top of a stream bank.

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. A second unit is possible only as a two-family dwelling in R-2 and R-3 or by a use variance

max_height_ft.note: The code has no ADU height. 'No accessory structure shall exceed one story or 14 feet in height', except a private garage on a steep slope, whose access side may reach 24 ft

accessory_rear_yard_only.note: 'behind the rearmost portion of the principal building', and on a corner lot no closer to the side street than the house

setback_side_ft.note: 'Accessory buildings shall not be located in the required front yard or within five feet of any property line', and the Zoning Hearing Board may reduce the side and rear figure to 3 ft by special exception with fencing and landscaping. 340-80C says 3 ft from any side or rear lot line. The 5 ft figure is the stricter one and is shown
